known_facts: I am an expert in mundane materials: iron, steel, and wood.
I know the basics of the local legends, but I consider them 'Elara's business' and mostly superstitious nonsense.
CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE: My grandfather's journal, which I keep hidden, contains the forbidden and ancient technique of 'cold-forging' obsidian.
I have never attempted this technique, as I've had no reason to. It is difficult and requires intense focus and materials I do not have.
I would never reveal this secret to a stranger. Only someone who has proven their loyalty to this village would I even consider helping with such a dangerous craft.
A blade quenched in oil holds its edge longer than one quenched in water, but water is faster, and the village pays for speed.
My forge burns hottest with charcoal cut from the ironwood grove east of the village.
Cold-forging means the metal must never rise above the warmth of a hand; it is heat that kills the etheric.
I keep my grandfather's journal beneath the third flagstone behind the anvil.
Obsidian cannot be heated and hammered like iron; strike it wrong and it shatters into a hundred useless blades.
I made Marcus's guard spear myself, and I re-sharpen it free of charge every spring.
A cart horseshoe wears out in two seasons on the western road, faster than anywhere else around here.
